title: The Joneses Visit an Economics Lab
abstract: arXiv:2607.07353v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Existing literature offers persuasive evidence that individuals care about how their consumption compares to that of peers, and proposes a large variety of explanatory models. The present paper proposes a common framework for many of those models, and compares their ability to predict behavior in a laboratory experiment. We find evidence of Keeping up with the Joneses motivations but also find that conspicuous consumption is enhanced by Veblen motivations arising from peers' ability to observe one's own choice. Among the seven quasi-linear preference models we compare, our data are best explained by a model that contrasts envy and pride (upward vs downward comparisons) using a value function borrowed from Prospect Theory.

translated_title: 琼斯一家造访经济学实验室
translated_abstract: 现有文献提供了令人信服的证据，表明个体关心自己的消费与同伴消费的比较，并提出了多种解释模型。本文为其中许多模型提出了一个统一框架，并通过实验室实验比较这些模型预测行为的能力。我们发现了“与邻里攀比”动机的证据，同时也发现，当同伴能够观察到自己的选择时，源于凡勃伦效应的动机会强化炫耀性消费。在我们比较的七个拟线性偏好模型中，实验数据最能被一个借鉴前景理论价值函数、对比嫉妒与自豪（即向上比较与向下比较）的模型所解释。
tldr: 本文为多种攀比消费模型建立了统一框架并在实验室中加以检验，发现同伴可观察性带来的凡勃伦动机强化了炫耀性消费，其中借鉴前景理论价值函数、对比嫉妒与自豪的模型最能解释实验数据。
